title: Calendar suite notifications: a cron releases lapsed Pencil holds, warns with a day left, and nudges a slipped to-do, and the co-host invite email reads as an invite

source.ref: Daniel, 2026-10-28: redesign the Space calendar with the Calendar system handoff (pass 8 of 9, notifications and the hold-release cron). Handoff spec 2.6 Hold lapse.

detail: Pass 8 of the Space calendar and project suite. /api/cron/calendar-holds runs hourly (:10), withCronHeartbeat, cronBudget, rejectUnauthorizedCron, off until CALENDAR_HOLDS_ENABLED (envFlag; blank in .env.example; activation gate in docs/RUNBOOKS.md 'Calendar holds'; a skipped run logs cron.calendar_holds.skipped). Each Space is looked at once a day in its own 9 AM (spaces.time_zone, else the platform home zone). It releases a Plan's hold when hold_until is before the Space's local today: a still-Pencil Plan has its unpublished Pencil dates soft-deleted (removed_at, recoverable), drops to stage plan and clears hold_until, conditional on the exact day it read so overlapping runs release once; a Plan that already moved on only clears the stale day. It warns the Plan owner with one day left and nudges the assignee of an open to-do that was due yesterday (one note per person per Space per day, only if they work that Space). Three registry rows (plan.hold_warning, plan.hold_released, plan.todo_overdue; lifecycle, push) route through routeNotification so the member's own push_lifecycle switch and a per-Space mute decide; sends carry an outbox dedupeKey. The co-host invite is the existing plan.share 'requested' email, re-voiced (buildPlanShareEmail). Pure rules in lib/calendar/hold-lapse-core.ts, IO in hold-lapse.ts. No migration. Not done: the release is not written to the Plan's edit history (space_plan_activity inserts are signed by a signed-in actor under RLS); it logs calendar.holds.released instead. Plan: /mnt/project-files/calendar-suite/PLAN.md.

verify.note: Fails on main (the route, the schedule entry, the registry rows and the runbook gate do not exist); passes here. The decisions themselves are proven by lib/calendar/hold-lapse-core.test.ts.
